title: "Resources"
order: 4

External links for this lesson. All checked to load from a plain browser request as of the date
this page was written. (Note: eCFR's and FDA's own sites block automated/proxied traffic with a
bot check, which is what this repo's build environment runs on, so a couple of the obvious first
choices — the eCFR page for this section, FDA's guidance-document database — can't be verified
from here even though a human browser reaches them fine. The regulation text quoted in this
lesson comes straight from eCFR's public API regardless; the first link below is a
verified-loading mirror of the same official text.)

- **[Cornell LII: 21 CFR 606.100, current text](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.100)**
  — Cornell Law School's Legal Information Institute mirrors the current CFR, including the
  section quoted in this lesson. Use this to check whether the SOP requirement has changed since
  this lesson was written; the dated snapshot in this repo's `sources/` folder won't update
  automatically. FDA's guidance-document database (search at fda.gov, under Regulatory
  Information) is the right place to pull the current version and issue date of the bacterial
  risk control strategies guidance referenced in this lesson before citing it in a real Lakeshore
  document — it just isn't linked directly here since this session couldn't confirm it loads.

- **[AABB: Standards & Accreditation](https://www.aabb.org/standards-accreditation/standards)**
  — AABB's own overview of its Standards program: what it covers, how standards are developed,
  and where accredited facilities fit in. Doesn't reproduce the (copyrighted) standards text
  itself, but confirms what the accreditation relationship actually is.

- **[CMS: Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA)](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/quality/clinical-laboratory-improvement-amendments)**
  — the federal program, run by CMS rather than FDA, that certifies laboratory testing quality.
  Relevant to the "who owns what" question this lesson touches on: a blood center's testing
  operations can fall under CLIA certification in addition to FDA blood regulation and AABB
  accreditation — three different oversight bodies, three different relationships.
